title: DPCexplorer Docker, Kubernetes, and GitHub CI/CD Deployment Plan

permanent_recommended.description: Two identical Django/Gunicorn containers in separate Kubernetes pods.

permanent_minimum.description: One Django/Gunicorn container, suitable for initial testing but without high availability.

postgresql.description: The application uses the PostgreSQL Service already available in the Kubernetes cluster.

temporary_per_release.description: A migration container runs as a Kubernetes Job and exits when migrations finish.

temporary_first_installation.description: A data-loader container populates the shared biological-data volume and then exits.

common_smoke_tests: A known protein ID search works.
A known Pfam ID search works.
A known DPCfam metacluster page works.
DPCfam FASTA, MSA, and HMM files are downloadable.
A known DPCstruct metacluster page works.
The 3D structure viewer loads a PDB file.
The large archive download links work.
Scientific tables remain read-only unless explicitly configured otherwise.
The liveness endpoint reports that Django is running.
The readiness endpoint confirms that PostgreSQL and biological-data storage are available.

milestones.name: Establish a working baseline
milestones.goal: Prove that the current application, database, and biological files work before changing deployment technology.
tasks: Run the current application normally.
Confirm that PostgreSQL contains the DPC scientific tables and Django auth, admin, and session tables.
Select one known protein ID, Pfam ID, DPCfam metacluster ID, and DPCstruct metacluster ID for repeatable testing.
Record the common smoke-test results.
completion_check: Run every common smoke test against the existing non-containerized application.
milestones.end_state: The existing application continues to work exactly as before.
milestones.rollback: No rollback is needed because this milestone does not change the application.

milestones.name: Make Django production-ready without Docker
milestones.goal: Prepare Django for production while it still runs directly from the Python virtual environment.
tasks: Add Gunicorn to requirements.txt.
Run the WSGI application with Gunicorn on port 8000.
Add /health/live for process health.
Add /health/ready to check PostgreSQL and a biological-data sentinel file.
Change logging from a local file to stdout.
Set DEBUG=False and configure ALLOWED_HOSTS.
Configure CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS for the production HTTPS URL.
Configure SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER for the Kubernetes Ingress.
Replace STATICFILES_STORAGE with Django's current STORAGES configuration.
Separate normal static assets from biological data by introducing DPC_DATA_ROOT and DPC_DATA_URL.
Run python manage.py check --deploy.
completion_check: Start the application with Gunicorn from the virtual environment.
Run every common smoke test.
Confirm that logs appear on stdout.
Confirm that readiness fails when PostgreSQL is unavailable.
Confirm that readiness fails when the biological-data directory is unavailable.
milestones.end_state: The complete application works in production mode without Docker.
milestones.rollback: Run the previous application revision using the original virtual-environment startup method.

milestones.name: Dockerize the application
milestones.goal: Run the complete application as one Docker container while using an external PostgreSQL database and mounted biological data.
tasks: Create a Dockerfile based on python:3.12-slim.
Install dependencies from requirements.txt.
Copy only application code and normal static assets.
Run collectstatic during the image build.
Create and use a non-root runtime user.
Start Gunicorn on 0.0.0.0:8000.
Create a .dockerignore file.
Exclude .venv, .git, logs, dataframes, downloads, production_files, notebooks, and profiling reports from the image.
Pass Django and PostgreSQL configuration through environment variables.
Mount the biological-data directory read-only at /data.
Do not include PostgreSQL in the application container.
Do not run setup_dpcexplorer_data.sh during every image build or container startup.
completion_check: Start one Docker container against the existing populated PostgreSQL database.
Run every common smoke test.
Restart the container and confirm that no application data is lost.
Confirm that stopping the container does not affect PostgreSQL.
Confirm that the image does not contain the approximately 40 GB generated data directory.
milestones.end_state: The complete application works from one portable Docker image.
milestones.rollback: Stop the container and start the working non-containerized Gunicorn deployment from milestone 1.

milestones.name: Deploy manually to Kubernetes
milestones.goal: Run the tested image in Kubernetes before giving GitHub permission to deploy.
tasks: Create or select a Kubernetes namespace for DPCexplorer.
Ask the database administrator to create a database and a dedicated least-privilege application user.
Transfer the working database with pg_dump and pg_restore, or load the project schema and datasets using the supplied scripts.
Use the Kubernetes PostgreSQL Service DNS name as DB_HOST.
Create an RWX PersistentVolumeClaim with approximately 60 to 70 GB capacity.
Populate the volume using a one-time, idempotent data-loader Job.
Create a /data/.dpcexplorer-data-ready sentinel after successful loading.
Mount the biological-data volume read-only at /data in every web pod.
Create a ConfigMap for non-secret settings.
Create a Secret for DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DB_PASSWORD.
Create a migration Job using the application image.
Create a Deployment, ClusterIP Service, and HTTPS Ingress.
Start with one replica and increase to two after verification.
Configure liveness and readiness probes.
Keep real secret values out of Git.
milestones.important_database_note: Django migrations create and update Django's own tables. They do not create the scientific tables because those models use managed=False.
completion_check: Run the migration Job and confirm that it completes.
Open the application through its HTTPS Ingress URL.
Run every common smoke test.
Delete one web pod and confirm that Kubernetes replaces it.
Confirm that the replacement pod uses the same database and data volume.
Scale to two replicas and confirm that both become ready.
Test a Kubernetes rollout rollback.
milestones.end_state: The complete application runs manually on Kubernetes without depending on GitHub deployment automation.
milestones.rollback: Use Kubernetes rollout undo or redeploy the previously verified image tag.

milestones.name: Add GitHub continuous integration
milestones.goal: Have GitHub validate changes and produce immutable images without automatically changing production.
tasks: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for pull requests and main.
Start a small temporary PostgreSQL service in CI.
Install dependencies.
Run Django system checks and tests.
Check that model changes have corresponding migrations.
Build the Docker image.
Start the image in CI and test the liveness endpoint.
Use a small test fixture rather than the complete biological dataset.
Push the image to GitHub Container Registry only after merging to main.
Tag images using the Git commit SHA.
Enable main-branch protection and require CI to pass.
completion_check: Open a test pull request with an intentional failure and confirm that GitHub blocks merging.
Fix the failure and confirm that CI passes.
Merge the pull request.
Confirm that an image tagged with the commit SHA exists in GHCR.
Manually deploy that exact image to Kubernetes.
Run every common smoke test against the deployed image.
milestones.end_state: GitHub produces verified images while Kubernetes deployment remains manual.

container_count.ci_containers: Temporary and only present on the GitHub Actions runner.

milestones.rollback: Continue running the previously deployed Kubernetes image if CI or image publication fails.

milestones.name: Add GitHub continuous deployment
milestones.goal: Automatically deploy an image that has already passed CI to Kubernetes.
tasks: Create a protected GitHub production Environment.
Require manual approval for production deployment.
Give GitHub a restricted Kubernetes identity that can manage only the DPCexplorer namespace.
Use a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner if the Kubernetes API is private.
Create a Kubernetes imagePullSecret if the GHCR image is private.
Deploy the exact image produced by CI without rebuilding it.
Run the migration Job and wait for it to succeed.
Update the Deployment to the commit-SHA image.
Wait for Kubernetes rollout status.
Call the readiness endpoint.
Run automatic known-ID smoke tests.
Mark the deployment successful only after all checks pass.
failure_rules: If migrations fail, do not update the web Deployment.
If new pods fail readiness, keep the old ready pods serving traffic.
If post-deployment smoke tests fail, roll back to the previous image SHA.
Do not automatically reverse database migrations.
completion_check: Make a harmless visible change in a pull request.
Let CI test and build the image.
Merge the pull request.
Approve the production deployment.
Confirm that the expected commit SHA is running.
Confirm that two replicas are ready.
Run every common smoke test.
Test rollback to the previous image SHA.
milestones.end_state: Approved changes are tested, published, migrated, deployed, and verified automatically.
milestones.rollback: Redeploy the previous immutable image SHA with Kubernetes rollout undo or the deployment workflow.

final_release_flow: Push the image to GHCR using the Git commit SHA.
Run readiness and functional smoke tests.
Keep or roll back the release based on the results.
